Data operations: residency, retention and DPDP in practice

After this lesson you can:
  • Apply the India-residency rules per data class
  • Operate retention, deletion and legal hold coherently
  • Handle breach duties: DPDP, CERT-In and RBI clocks together

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Residency is per data class, not per server
  2. Retention: keep, then provably stop keeping
  3. When it goes wrong: three clocks at once
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Residency is per data class, not per server

Saying 'we host in India' is not the control. Each data class carries its own rule:

  • Digital-lending personal data — stored on India servers; if processed abroad, deleted there and returned within 24 hours.
  • Payment-system data — India-only storage where in scope.
  • V-CIP recordings and logs — India-stored, full stop.
  • Aadhaar biometrics/OTP/PID — nowhere, ever (module 2).

LoanOS models residency as metadata on data classes with vendor-routing consequences: an integration that would move a restricted class offshore fails validation. A BA adding any integration must classify its data flows first — that classification is the requirement.

2. Retention: keep, then provably stop keeping

Every class also carries a retention schedule by product and legal basis — KYC records and transaction evidence under PMLA/RBI rules (years after relationship end), complaint files, audit evidence.

The other edge: DPDP expects data not to be kept beyond purpose.

The reconciliation is module 2's erasure-with-hold pattern plus automated deletion/anonymisation when retention lapses, and legal hold freezing deletion when litigation or investigation intervenes.

Proof of deletion is itself evidence.

3. When it goes wrong: three clocks at once

A serious security incident at a lender trips parallel duties: CERT-In — report qualifying cyber incidents within 6 hours (a duty LoanOS carries directly as an Indian service provider, alongside 180-day India log retention and NTP-synchronised clocks); RBI — the RE's incident-notification duties under IT-outsourcing directions, which the platform's contracts must support within the RE's 6-hour window; DPDP — breach notification to the Data Protection Board and affected individuals per the Rules' timelines. The platform's incident workflow is built to feed all three from one evidence trail — a BA designing incident-adjacent features should assume every artefact may end up in front of three different authorities.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-DATA-RESIDENCY — India storage for digital-lending personal data; 24-hour return rule.
  • RBI-PAY-DATA — Payment-system data India-only storage.
  • CERT-IN-2022 — 6-hour incident reporting, 180-day India log retention, NTP sync.
  • DPDP-RULES-2025 — Breach assessment and notification duties under phased commencement.
  • RBI-IT-OUTSOURCE-2023 — The platform must support the RE's own incident and audit duties as its IT provider.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability CON-009 — Retention schedules by data class, product and legal basis.
  • Capability CON-010 — Automated deletion, anonymisation and legal hold.
  • Capability CON-014 — Data-breach notification to Board and affected principals.
  • Capability SEC-016 — CERT-In log retention and trusted time synchronization.
  • Document docs/architecture/data-governance.md — Data classes, residency and governance architecture.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Digital-lending personal data is processed by an offshore service. What must happen?

  1. Nothing if encrypted
  2. Deleted offshore and brought back to India within 24 hours
  3. Kept offshore with consent
  4. Anonymised offshore
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. The residency rule permits offshore processing only with deletion abroad and 24-hour return — a hard integration constraint.

2. Which incident clock applies to LoanOS itself, not just its RE customers?

  1. The RBI 6-hour RE window only
  2. CERT-In's 6-hour reporting duty as an Indian service provider
  3. DPDP only
  4. None — vendors are exempt
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. CERT-In directions bind Indian service providers directly; the platform is inside the regulatory perimeter, not behind it.
